messages.content: Help me update the property 'version' of an object named 'packageInfo' to '1.2.3', ensuring the update only occurs if the new value differs from the existing one or if 'version' is not already a property of the object?

function.name: vOe
function.description: This function updates a property of an object to a new value, but only if the new value is different from the existing one or if the property does not already exist on the object. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

r.description: The object to update. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

e.description: The property of the object to update. This is JavaScript String type parameter in string representation.

t.description: The new value to assign to the property. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function vOe with parameters r (object), e (property name), t (new value). Provide them as strings. So we need to pass JSON string representations. For example:

{
  "r": "{\"name\":\"my-package\",\"description\":\"A sample package\"}",
  "e": "\"version\"",
  "t": "\"1.2.3\""
}

But we don't know the current state of packageInfo. We just need to provide the function call. The user didn't give the current object. We could assume it's empty or has some properties. But we should ask for the current object? The instruction says "Help me update the property 'version' of an object named 'packageInfo' to '1.2.3', ensuring the update only occurs if the new value differs from the existing one or if 'version' is not already a property of the object?" So we need to call the function with the object. But we don't have the object. Maybe we can create a placeholder like "{}" and let the function handle it. But the function will check if property exists and if new value differs. If object doesn't have version, it will add it.

Thus we can call with r: "{}", e: "\"version\"", t: "\"1.2.3\"" . That will add version property.
